Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:14: And he says further there, the "hevels" of the Other Side, of them it is said (Jeremiah 10:15), "they are vanity, a work of delusion" - for those "hevels" ascend through vulgar speech and falsehoods, and they all ascend to the brain - there is a sun, moon, stars, and constellations in the firmaments that are the husks, of which it is said (Isaiah 5:18), "woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood," and of them it is said (ibid. 51:6), "for the heavens shall vanish like smoke," "the moon shall be ashamed and the sun confounded" (ibid. 24:23), and they have many "hevels," all full of falsehood and vanity - and whoever utters false words, how many destroying angels open their wings to receive them - this is what is written (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" - and these utterances are the sons of several buildings - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:15: Behold, it is explained in these teachings the difference between the holy "hevel" from the occupation with Torah and the like, and the unholy "hevel," for the unholy "hevel" ascends to the husk and builds vain buildings - "vanity, a work of delusion" - as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:16: The general rule is that as a person builds in this world, there his soul ascends after his death, as explained in the teaching from Parashat Beshalach that we copied - unless he repents fully and strongly, to nullify all those firmaments and lands he built on the side of the husk.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:17: And so he says further there in the Tikkunim (page 118a), that all the "hevels" of prayers ascend and bind to the holy "hevel," which is the Shechinah, and there is a "hevel" of idle words, and it is in the husk - in these words, in brief: there is "hevel" of which it is said (Genesis 4:2), "his brother, Hevel [Abel]," and there is "hevel" in prayers and good service, and there is "hevel" of idle words, empty words, of which it is said, "vanity, a work of delusion," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:18: And further there he explains that between these two "hevels" there is a middle "hevel," which is neither holy nor impure, but rather ordinary conversation, which is the need to use the matters of this world - concerning this we say, "who separates between holy and profane," and concerning the external "hevel" we say, "and between Israel and the other nations."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:19: Now, when a person considers what we wrote above, that a person is obligated to sanctify his limbs because in every single limb of his the Name YHVH is found, and in sanctifying that limb he sanctifies the Name - all the more so is he obligated to sanctify his mouth, in which the Name YHVH is found in several aspects, whether in the limbs that produce speech, and the five points of articulation participate in producing speech, and it is necessary that the Name YHVH be in each and every one, since they are distinct organs - throat, palate, tongue, teeth, lips - or in the aspect of voice and speech itself, in which the Name YHVH is found, as explained above. And so it is fitting that he consider that in prayer he utters several mentions [of the divine Name] from his mouth, whether in psalms or in blessings, and therefore it is fitting to sanctify his mouth, so that the Name YHVH not go out through a blemished mouth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:20: And in the Tikkunim (page 132a) it says, in these words: a crooked mouth - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest in it, for it is a blemish; all the more so its crooked speech, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:15), "what is crooked cannot be made straight." Mouth and heart correspond to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah - voice and speech that emerge from both are Vav-Heh, which must be brought forth in the fear and love of Yud-Heh, and if not, YHVH does not rest there - to this point. And what he says, "mouth and heart correspond to Torah," the intent is that the heart is the Written Torah and the mouth corresponds to the Oral Torah - for just as the mouth reveals what is hidden in the heart, so the Oral Torah reveals what is concealed in the Written Torah. And the intent of this is to teach us that his mouth and his heart should be equal, and through this he unifies - but if he speaks one thing with his mouth and another with his heart, he separates and "cuts the shoots."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:21: And from the sum of the teaching it is understood that wherever there is a blemish in his mouth or his speech, the Name YHVH does not rest there, and he shall be obligated to come into transmigration (according to what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, taught us, as mentioned above) to repair what he twisted. And just as the punishment is great, so the reward of one who sanctifies his mouth is great, for he sanctifies the Shechinah, called "mouth," and therefore he merits the holy spirit, as we explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:22: And concerning profane speech, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, warned us in the Mishnah, saying (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 17), "I have found nothing better for the body than silence" - and "for the body" is explained as, for the affairs of the body, as they said, of blessed memory, in Chullin (89a), on the verse (Psalms 58:2), "do you indeed speak righteousness in silence [elem]," in these words: Rabbi Yitzchak said, what is the meaning of "do you indeed speak righteousness in silence, do you judge uprightly, O sons of men"? What is a person's craft in this world? Let him make himself as one silent [as an "elem"]. One might think even concerning words of Torah - therefore Scripture says, "speak righteousness." One might think he should be arrogant - therefore Scripture says, "judge uprightly, O sons of men" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:23: And so King Solomon, peace be upon him, warned us concerning this and said (Ecclesiastes 5:1), "do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth, therefore let your words be few." And it must be examined how it gives the reason for words being few as being that "God is in heaven and you are on earth" - for on the contrary, this indicates the removal of providence, and it should rather have said words indicating providence - "for God is in heaven and on earth" - along the lines of (Psalms 113:6), "who humbles Himself to behold the things that are in heaven and on earth." And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Sifrei (Ha'azinu 4): Solomon said, if even the weakest of the weak above overcomes the mighty, when he is below and He above, all the more so is He the mightiest of the mighty - and so it says (Deuteronomy 32:6), "do you thus repay the LORD" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:24: However, what appears to us in explaining this verse - even if it be lengthy - because of the great benefit reaching the tongue from it, we shall not be concerned about length. It is this: one must examine precisely the words "al tevahel al picha" - it should have said "al tevahel picha" or "et picha" - what is the "al" [upon/about]?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:25: Rather, the matter is that the mouth comprises the five points of articulation of the letters, and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 132a), in these words: there are five repairs in the mouth, of which it is said in Sefer Yetzirah, Alef-Chet-Heh-Ayin, Bet-Vav-Mem-Peh, Gimel-Yud-Chaf-Kuf, Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Tav, Zayin-Samech-Shin-Resh-Tzadi - and through them complete stones shall be built for the Holy One, blessed be He, in several prayers and services, and concerning them Jacob said (Genesis 28:11), "and he lay down in that place [vayishkav bamakom hahu]" - "vayishkav" is "Vav-Yud-Shin-Kaf-Bet" [could be parsed as] "Yesh-Kaf-Bet" [Yud-Shin, Kaf-Bet], "in that place" - "Yesh" - "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance [yesh]" (Proverbs 8:21); "Kaf-Bet" - "in you [bekha] shall Israel bless" (Genesis 48:20) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:26: And in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 2, mishnah 6) it says that the Holy One, blessed be He, fixed in our mouth twenty-two letters at five points of articulation - twenty-two foundation letters, engraved in voice, hewn in breath, fixed in the mouth at five places: Alef-Chet-Heh-Ayin, Bet-Vav-Mem-Peh, Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Tav, Zayin-Samech-Tzadi-Resh-Shin, Gimel-Yud-Chaf-Kuf. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that the word "fixed in the mouth," said there, teaches us a great matter - namely, that the reality of the five points of articulation is rooted very high, in the head, and they are the root of all existing things, as explained in the Idra - however, they descend and are revealed from world to world in the aspects of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His love for man, fixed these letters in his mouth so that he might be able to cleave to his Creator - for in mentioning these letters below, in his Torah or his prayer, he shakes and arouses above the supernal roots - and this is the word "fixed" [kava], which is like one who fastens a chain, one end in one place and its other end in another place - for even if that place is distant, when a person shakes the end of the chain in his hand, he shakes the whole chain, however large it may be. And so he also says at the end of Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 6, mishnah 8), "he bound the twenty-two letters on his tongue, and the Omnipresent revealed to him His secret" - and the word "bound" [kesher] also indicates what is being expounded in the word "kava" [fixed].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:27: And through this we shall understand the virtue of the early ones, peace be upon them, whose prayer was answered immediately, because they were careful not to blemish the twenty-two letters, which are the five points of articulation fixed in their mouths, with idle talk and the other things that blemish the tongue - therefore their prayer would split the firmaments and ascend higher and higher to arouse mercy - and so it says in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 14b) that at the time Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, was occupied with Torah, several thousands and tens of thousands of ministering angels would hear his voice - and the reason is that because the points of articulation emerging from their mouths were pure, they would bind and unify all the worlds, for the voice and speech emerging from their mouths would become satisfaction above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:28: However, when there is a blemish in the five points of articulation, the breath of prayer and Torah emerging from his mouth emerges with a blemish and adhesion, and it is impossible for it to be unified above, for "whoever has a blemish shall not approach" (Leviticus 21:18) - and so it says in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 227b), in these words: and just as those five wings of the lung are all open without adhesion, to receive this voice, so too the five repairs of the mouth must all be open without adhesion, in the five repairs which are: Alef-Chet-Heh-Ayin in the throat, Bet-Vav-Mem-Peh in the lips, Gimel-Yud-Chaf-Kuf in the palate, Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Tav in the tongue, Zayin-Samech-Shin-Resh-Tzadi in the teeth - and let the speech that is in them be without adhesion and hindrance at all - this is what is written (Genesis 24:15), "and it came to pass, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebecca came out" - this is prayer, which is speech, and concerning it is said, "if my prayer is fluent in my mouth, I know it is accepted; and if there is adhesion and it comes out mixed, I know it is unfit," because adhesion is a "treifah" [invalidating flaw] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:29: Now, with this introduction, we shall understand the verse, in saying "al tevahel al picha" - and the intent is that your mouth comprises the five points of articulation explained. And "tevahel" [be rash/confused] means that no blemish be found in them, which is "behalah" [confusion] and husk, and the husk is external - it is "al picha" [upon your mouth], which is extraneous and comes upon the five points of articulation. And my colleague, his honor Rabbi Moshe Biarokash, peace be upon him, said something fine concerning this - that it is known (Parashat Naso, page 134a) that from the supernal mouth emerges "hevel" [breath], as we explained above, and it means, "do not be rash" - that you not transform "hevel" [breath] into "behalah" [confusion], which is the husk.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:30: Now, along the lines of explaining "al picha," they explained, of blessed memory, in Tanchuma, of blessed memory: this is what Scripture says, "do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word" - these are people who curse the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Come and see, when the higher and lower beings were created, they were created with half the Name, as it is said (Isaiah 26:4), "for in Yah, the LORD, is an everlasting rock" - and why were they not created with the whole [Name]? Because the world is not worthy that the whole Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, be mentioned. Woe to the creatures who curse the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He - see what is written concerning offerings: "an offering to the LORD," "a burnt offering to the LORD" - it does not say "to the LORD, an offering; to the LORD, a burnt offering" - yet people curse and blaspheme My Name - therefore it is said, "do not be rash with your mouth." This explicitly teaches that they came to explain the word "al tevahel" through "al" [upon] - for the "behalah" [rashness] is the cursing and blaspheming, and it is extraneous, upon the mouth - which a person has no need of, for his mouth, certainly, was created for the need of the five points of articulation within it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:31: And it is further possible to say - it is known that the speech that comes to a person is from the Shechinah, as it is said (Exodus 4:11), "who has made man's mouth, or who makes him dumb," and so on, "is it not I, the LORD?" - and the word "Anochi" [I] can be explained as the supernal Shechinah and the lower Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 74b), that concerning them it is said "Anochi Anochi" - but the main one is the supernal Shechinah, from where it is "Anochi Adonai Elohecha" [I am the LORD your God], as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 256b) - and this means, do not blemish the measure that is "al picha" [upon your mouth], from where it came to be a mouth, for the five points of articulation are from the secret of the supernal Heh, and from there too the power of speech, as it is said, "or who makes him dumb," and so on. And if we explain this concerning the Shechinah, "and she is upon your mouth," we explain "is it not I, the LORD," as voice and speech - and the rest of the particulars of the verse also fit these measures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:32: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that a person's mouth is above ten [handbreadths], and if the voice and speech emerging from his mouth are in holiness, the Shechinah is immediately bound to it, for the Shechinah does not descend below ten [handbreadths] (Sukkah 5a). And along these lines the wording of the verse "al picha" is now precise, that the Shechinah is "upon your mouth," since your mouth is above ten [handbreadths] - and this is (Psalms 68:14), "though you lie among the sheepfolds [shefatayim]," which is explained in the Tikkunim (page 45a) as, that he should lay the Shechinah, who is "Em" [mother], between his lips ["sefatayim"], in order to unify her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:33: Further, we already copied in the Gate of Love, chapter 9, what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, said in his precepts (Zohar, Parashat Naso, page 122b), that the Shechinah is "the utterance of the mouth of the LORD," through whom man is sustained, in these words, in brief: and she is the breath that enters a person's mouth without toil and without effort - Heh, "when they were created." And in this teaching "al picha" fits well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:34: "And let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God" - the matter is that speech emerges from the heart, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna several times (Parashat Naso, page 121b; Parashat Pinchas, page 227b), and in the Tikkunim (page 28a), in these words: the heart is a consuming fire, from the right ear of the heart, which corresponds to the liver, and from it speech emerges - this is what is written (Jeremiah 23:29), "is not My word like fire, says the LORD" - and were it not for the wings of the lung that fan upon the heart, it would burn up the whole body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:35: And therefore it says, "and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word," for from it speech emerges, and the speech emerging from it is judgment, as Rashbi explained, that the heart is fire, and concerning speech it is said, "is not My word like fire." And speech emerges "before God," which is judgment - for the essence of this world was created with judgment, as it is said (Genesis 1:1), "in the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth" - and when He saw that it could not endure, He joined with it the attribute of mercy (cf. Bereshit Rabbah 12:15) - however, this is only a joining in some measure, for its essence was created with judgment and stands upon judgment, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, page 30b), that every single day judgment hangs over the world, because the world was created and stands upon judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:36: And it is possible to say, in another way, concerning "before God," to teach us of providence, and that he should know that when he speaks, the King of kings of kings, God, hears our words - and as Rambam, peace be upon him, explained concerning fear (Guide for the Perplexed, part 3, chapter 52), that a person does not prolong his words before a king as he does when he is in his own house - and the King of kings of kings' regard is constantly upon us, and therefore it says, "let not... be hasty," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:37: However, one must examine precisely, for ultimately this verse appears redundant in its matter - for "do not be rash with your mouth" means that he should not let speech out of his mouth quickly, and this is the same as "and let not your heart be hasty," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:38: Therefore it appears that these are two divisions: the first concerning worldly matters and the second concerning matters of holiness. Concerning what pertains to worldly matters it says, "do not be rash with your mouth" - meaning that although you have permission to speak, this being "your mouth," which is in your own domain, it should not be with rashness and haste, but with calm composure. And even concerning matters of holiness, when you stand before God, "do not be hasty to utter a word before God" - and so it is explained in the Talmud (Berachot, chapter 5, mishnah 1), that one should not pray immediately, but settle his mind first and know before whom he stands, as they said, "one may only stand to pray in a state of gravity," and so on. And so it says in the Midrash (Yalkut Shmuel 2, chapter 7, siman 146) that David said, I would not pray before God until I had settled my mind - and we shall copy his whole wording below concerning the matter of prayer, with God's help. And even in the occupation with Torah, one must sit in awe and direct his intent to what he utters from his mouth, as we shall elaborate in its place. And in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 2a) it says that a word is worth a sela, but silence two [selas] - this applies even concerning Torah. And this is "and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God" - meaning, when you stand before the Shechinah, which is when he is occupied with Torah and prayer, let him not be hasty.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:39: "For God is in heaven and you are on earth" - it is known that "Elohim" is a term of judgment and a judge, as they explained, of blessed memory (Shemot Rabbah 3:6), "when I judge My world I am called Elohim." And in saying "in heaven," it means that He judges in heaven with the whole heavenly retinue that is in heaven - and therefore it did not say "for God is above the heavens," which would indicate His removal and elevation from them, but rather "in heaven" is to watch over and judge, as (Psalms 103:19), "the LORD has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all." Further, "Elohim" totals the numerical value of "ha-kisei" [the throne] - and this means that His throne, from which He judges, is in heaven, and the angels before Him, some on the right for merit, some on the left for guilt - and since, when a person speaks, the Holy One, blessed be He, judges his words with the whole heavenly retinue, whether his words are upright or not, it is fitting that they be few, in order to minimize the judgment upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:40: And therefore it says everything in the term "Elohim," for everything is judged with strict judgment, without leniency in anything - and as they said in the Midrash, Vayikra Rabbah (Parashat Emor 26:7), in these words: Rabbi would recite the verse, and when he reached this verse he would weep: "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his speech [sicho]" (Amos 4:13). What is "declares to man what is his speech"? Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Ye'avetz said, "who forms the mountains and creates the wind." Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Ye'avetz said another interpretation: "tohu, choshech, va'afelah" [chaos, darkness, and gloom] - even matters that have no substance, even light conversation a person converses with his wife, are written on a person's record and read before him at the time of his death. And who writes them? "He who makes the dawn darkness" (Amos, ibid.) - to this point, their wording. And the reason speech is written by the blessed Name is because speech is through the soul, as it is written (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul," and we translate [in the Targum], "and man became a speaking spirit" - and it is known that the soul is from Him, blessed be He, as it is written (ibid.), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" - and therefore, since the essence of the soul is what blemishes through speech or is repaired through good speech, everything is written by Him, blessed be He, in order to punish it or reward it, measure for measure, according to His blessed knowledge, which is not known to any creature, not to an angel and not to a seraph.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:41: "And you are on earth" - it is precise in saying "and you are on earth," and not "and you are in the earth," along the lines of saying "for God is in heaven," to answer for us the difficulty we examined above. And the matter is that man's primary dwelling, before the sin of the first man, was in the Garden of Eden, removed from the coarse materiality of this turbid body - however, through his sin he was clothed in the body and matter of this world, and behold, according to his understanding he is separated from holiness. However, there the Holy One, blessed be He, placed in man, at the beginning of his creation, speech, beyond all the living creatures of this world, for through speech he is equal to the angels - and as explained above, the matter of the three bonds that are in man, nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah, which are deed, speech, thought - and Rashbi explained that speech is from the holy living creatures, which is the level of ru'ach (Tikkunei Zohar, page 68b) - and through speech there is power in man to cleave to holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:42: And this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, intended in saying (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth" - for man, from the aspect of the speech within him, his spirit ascends upward, while the beast's spirit descends downward, because it returns to its foundation in "Asiyah" [mere doing], since the power of speech was not placed in it, which is a divine power given to man, as it says (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul," and we translate, "and man became a speaking spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:43: And this is what it says, "and you are 'al' [upon/removed from] the earth" - for from the aspect of the soul and speech within you, you are removed from the earth and from its matter, meaning that you are not equal to the other living creatures of the earth. And therefore, when a person speaks, whether words of holiness or of the profane, he should not think that he is speaking on earth and that he is physical, but rather that he is spiritual, speaking with the angels, for in speech he is equal to them. And therefore the verse did not need to say "for God is in heaven and on earth," for where it would say that His providence is on earth, that is to watch over the deeds done on earth from the aspect of the material deed - but concerning speech, man is bound above, and immediately upon uttering speech he is "before God," for this God is in heaven. And this is the precision of the verse, "do not be hasty to utter a word before God" - and since "before God" might imply one who dwells on earth, it guards against this and says that God, whom I told you is in heaven - and you, when you utter speech, are removed from the earth ["al ha-aretz"] - it follows that you are speaking before God in heaven, for the reason stated.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:44: "Therefore let your words be few" - since you stand above, before the King, it is not fitting that you prolong your words before Him. And it is precise in saying "your words" - meaning the words of the body, which are yours, and not the Holy One, blessed be He's - but words of praise, prayer, and Torah, which are His, the King desires that they always be before Him, to prolong His praises and meditate on His Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:45: And we have necessity for the reality of this introduction from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that speech has this virtue more than other commandments a person performs - for the other things a person does in deed, there are seven, "the eyes of the LORD roam through all the earth," as explained in the Sabba, Parashat Mishpatim (page 107a), concerning (Psalms 51:6), "and have done evil in Your sight" - that they go about the world and through them every commandment or transgression a person performs is imprinted. However, concerning speech, Rashbi explained that the voice itself ascends above and is examined there, so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha (page 92a), in these words: Rabbi Yosi opened (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous," and so on - happy is Israel, more than all the other nations, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, called righteous - for we have learned, one hundred twenty-eight thousand masters of wings go about and fly through the whole world, and hear a voice and take hold of that voice - as we have learned, there is no matter in the world that has no voice, and it goes and flies in the firmament, and the masters of wings take hold of it and raise that voice to their Masters of judgment, and they judge it, whether for good or for evil, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice," and so on - to this point. Behold, they said that every utterance has a voice and ascends above into the firmament, and from there the masters of wings take the matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:46: And in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 55a), on the verse (Psalms 17:1), "hear, O LORD, my just cause," and so on, "without lips of deceit" - they add and say that the voice itself ascends and splits the firmament, they said, of blessed memory: what is "without lips of deceit"? Rather, we have learned this: every single word a person utters from his mouth ascends above and splits the firmaments and enters the place it enters, and there that word is examined, whether it is a fit word or not - if it is a fit word, they bring it before the holy King to do His will; and if not, they turn it aside to the Other Side, to arouse another spirit through that word - to this point. And so he explained at the beginning of Parashat Naso, and we shall copy it below, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:47: And so in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, page 31b), it says there that a matter dependent on speech arouses speech above, and it says, in these words: and should you say, what does a word arouse? Rather, so it is written (Job... "davar dibber"), that word arouses another word above, and it is called "davar" - "the word [devar] of the LORD which was," "and the word of the LORD was precious," "by the word of the LORD the heavens were made" - for we have learned, that word ascends and splits the firmaments until it ascends to its place and arouses what it arouses - if good, good; if evil, evil - as it is written (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every [evil] word," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:48: However, a difficulty for this matter arises from what is explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of page 131), that there are angels called "masters of wings," appointed over the voices of Torah, in these words: and there are precepts that depend on the mouth, appointed over the voices of Torah and over the utterances of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and a possessor of wings shall tell the matter" - to this point. And he says further there (page 72), and the angels of whom it is said "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" depend on voice, and "a possessor of wings shall tell the matter" depends on speech - to this point. And this is difficult - since the voice ascends and splits the firmament of itself, why would these angels be needed?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:49: And it may be said that this ascending voice certainly has some physical aspect from the side of the person, who is in this physical "Asiyah," and therefore the masters of wings take hold of it in order to refine it through them, so that it ascend to the fitting place - if it is a breath of Torah or prayer, that it ascend higher and higher to unify; and if the ascending voice is a voice concerning worldly matters, they judge it according to need. And with this answer we must also explain what they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 201b), that there are several angels who raise the prayer from firmament to firmament - why would they be needed? Rather, certainly in order to refine it from physicality, so that it ascend higher and higher to unify.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:50: Further, it is possible to say "for God is in heaven," as it is written in the Ra'aya Meheimna (page 258a), in the secret of the Name Elohim, in these words: "Elohim" testifies to His divinity, that there is "Elohim" and "the God of gods," and He is God over all and there is no god over Him - to this point. And "in heaven" shall be understood by what is said in the Tikkunim (end of page 3), that the Cause over all shines in the ten sefirot of Atzilut, and so on, and in the ten spheres of the firmament, and does not change in any place. And this is the intent of saying "for God is in heaven" - meaning that His divinity and His light shine in all the heavens as one, in one equality, as it says, "that shines in the ten spheres of the firmament," and so on - and now this certainly indicates providence.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:51: Further, it is possible that "for God is in heaven" - for it is known that "Elohim" is the supernal Imma, and her dwelling is in "heaven," which are the three Patriarchs - and the intent is that she decrees no decree except through a court of three, which are the three Patriarchs, so that the matter be judged to the right and to the left, and afterward the third decides - and along this pattern, a person who is on earth must, when he utters a matter, first weigh it in the scales of the intellect, to the right and to the left, and to a decision - and through this his words shall be few. And further I have hidden matters concerning this verse, written with me, and it suffices with what we have elaborated for practical benefit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:52: Now, the particular aspects explained in this verse obligate a person to minimize his words - whether in the aspect of the secret of "hevel" explained, or in the aspect of the five points of articulation fixed in his mouth, that there be no adhesion in them, or in the aspect of voice and speech, or in the aspect of the refinement of the voice and speech that ascend above to be judged, as explained, or in the aspect of the constant providence upon him - he must minimize his words in worldly matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:53: And with this the chapter is concluded:
